moduleTitle: Creating custom action steps with Copilot in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Use Testim Copilot to generate a custom action step's JavaScript from a plain-text description.
Use the Coding Assistant's Explain and Fix commands to understand and repair existing custom-step code.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Generating custom steps with generative AI

elements.description: Copilot proposes JavaScript for supported coded steps from prompts. The response is a draft, not a guarantee of a working or correct test; review the intended action or assertion and runtime.

Open Write code with AI on a supported step and acknowledge the notice. Slash commands include Generate, Explain, Fix and Help. Generated or fixed code appears in chat; Paste code at cursor or Copy code inserts it deliberately.

elements.title: The Coding Assistant's three core commands
items: Generate — produce new custom-step JavaScript from a plain-text description.
Explain — select existing JavaScript and get a readable description of what it does.
Fix — analyze code that's producing an error and get a suggested fix.

bulletPoints: Testim Copilot generates custom-step JavaScript from a plain-text description.
Write code with AI → acknowledge notice → Generate/Explain/Fix/Help; insert generated/fixed drafts explicitly.
This lowers the JavaScript bar for testers who aren't primarily developers, without removing the option to hand-edit the result.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming Copilot-generated code needs no review
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Accepting AI-generated custom-step code without reading or testing it, on the assumption that generative AI output is automatically correct.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Review and test the draft against the requirement. Explain and Fix are suggestions, not proof of correctness; inspect the actual code and execution results.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does the 'Generate' command in Testim Copilot's Coding Assistant do?

options.text: Deletes unused custom steps from the project.
Creates new custom-step JavaScript automatically from a plain-text description.
Converts a custom step into a built-in predefined step.
Runs the test suite and generates a report.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's about writing new code from a description, not managing existing steps.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Generate proposes JavaScript from the prompt. The user inserts, reviews and tests that draft; a chat response is not automatic installation or execution success.

optionExplanations.B: It proposes code from a prompt for review and deliberate insertion.
optionExplanations.C: It does not automatically turn a coded step into a built-in step.
optionExplanations.D: Code generation is distinct from suite execution/reporting.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester inherits a custom action step with confusing JavaScript and no comments. Which Coding Assistant command helps them understand what it does?
practiceQuiz.hint: They need a description of existing code, not new code or a bug fix.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Explain describes selected code. Validate that description against the code and runtime behavior; Generate proposes new code and Fix proposes changes.

optionExplanations.A: Generate proposes new code rather than explaining the selected code.
optionExplanations.C: Fix proposes changes for selected code.
optionExplanations.D: Reassign changes an AUT target, not explains code.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How is the Coding Assistant opened for a custom step?

options.text: By clicking 'Write code with AI' after creating the custom step.
It opens automatically for every step in the test.
By right-clicking the test name in the Test Library.
Through the project's Settings > API page.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a button specific to custom code steps.
practiceQuiz.rationale: For a supported step, Write code with AI opens the assistant after acknowledging its notice. Slash commands provide assistance; insertion and validation of drafts remain deliberate user actions.

optionExplanations.A: Write code with AI is the documented supported-step entry point.
optionExplanations.B: The assistant is not automatically opened for every step.
optionExplanations.C: Library context menus are not the documented code-assistant entry point.
optionExplanations.D: Project API settings are not that entry point.

quickRecap.value: Proposes custom-step JavaScript drafts from prompts; review and test them.
Supported step → Write code with AI → acknowledge notice; insert the draft deliberately.
Generate proposes code; Explain describes selected code; Fix suggests changes; Help opens documentation.
